title: Consolidate load + eval pipelines into a single deterministic perf harness
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Replace the ad-hoc mix of load scripts, flaky sampling tests, and isolated eval runners with a single, maintainable perf harness that can (1) run deterministic replay workloads for regression detection, (2) produce CI-friendly artifacts (latency histograms, token-level cost summaries, KV cache hit/miss), and (3) drive nightly and on-demand load jobs across hosted/dedicated/private clusters.

Scope and deliverables:
- Implement a deterministic input replay layer that records request traces from production-like traffic and replays them with throttled timing and KV-cache warmup phases.
- Consolidate existing scripts (locust and custom Python runners) into a k6-based harness for load and a small Go helper for KV-cache simulation where needed.
- Add golden prompt sets and a configuration schema (YAML) for per-model perf profiles (seq len distribution, top-k/top-p sampling seeds) so regression runs are reproducible.
- Replace flaky end-to-end sampling checks with metric-based regression assertions (p95/p99 latency, throughput, token cost delta, and hallucination-rate measured by eval harness hooks).
- Integrate harness as a new pipeline job in GitHub Actions and in the internal perf scheduler to run nightly for mainline models and on-demand for model rollouts.
- Provide a migration guide and small compatibility shims to import historical traces used by ENG-4827/ENG-8392.

Acceptance criteria:
- Successful deterministic replay of three representative workloads (chat interactive, long-context seq, embeddings bulk) with <5% run-to-run variability in median latency after warmup.
- CI job that executes a short regression suite and fails the PR if p99 latency increases >10% or cost-per-token rises >7% against the pinned baseline.
- Nightly job artifacts available in S3 + Dashboard link showing the last 14 days of histograms and KV cache stats.
- Docs: Confluence page with harness design, migration steps, and example config; sample PR that migrates one existing locust job to k6.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not include a full rewrite of the eval scoring models (only instrumentation and hooks).
- It does not change production routing logic or rollout policies (those are separate initiatives).

Risks and trade-offs:
- Moving to k6 increases reliability for load generation but requires rewriting some Python-only generators; mitigated by providing Python compatibility wrappers during migration.
- Deterministic replays require seeding sampling behavior; this reduces behavioral diversity in tests (intentional) but we will keep a separate stochastic suite for coverage.

Rollout plan:
1) Prototype deterministic replay + k6 wrapper (week 1).
2) Add KV-cache simulation helper and golden prompt sets (week 2).
3) Wire CI and nightly jobs, add dashboards (week 3).
4) Migrate two non-critical locust jobs and retire originals (week 4).

Metrics to monitor post-rollout:
- Run-to-run variability (median latency standard deviation)
- False-positive regression rate on CI
- Flakiness rate in nightly runs (number of aborted jobs)
- Time to onboard new models into perf harness (target <2 hours)
